statement: Fear is a subject in 5 of the analysed books with four different handlings: Brave Bora names it and a parent supports him; AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! has an adult name each scare and reframe it as ordinary; Bohlale names it herself and defuses it by looking again; Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! has the child name it and two friends support him; Good Night, Monu shows it only in pictures and the child settles it alone.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-15: Bohlale (African Storybook): scary eyes 4/5, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale, defused on the next page. Monu (StoryWeaver): 4/5 over three pages, about 2 on 0-3. In neither does an adult support the child at the fear peak.
2026-11-13: +1 support (Mmawe: adult names and reframes, 4/5 at the fourth scream, about 3 on the engine's 0-3 scale, which the engine forbids at 5-6; the book is 3-4), +1 counter (Khuzwayo: peers, not a parent, support him; fear 4/5, about 2 on 0-3, reduced not removed). Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Trip to the Tap (2023), Going Places (2025), AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! (2024), Can We Eat a Rainbow? (2026), I Can Do It! (2026), Play with Me (2026), Banzi's Busy Bees (2025), Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! (2023), Alex's Super Medicine (2022); StoryWeaver — Sweet Dreams (Pratham Books, year not shown).

magicpaper.current: fear, panic, grief, despair (intensity 3) never permitted at age 5-6
magicpaper.suggested: Open question, not a recommendation: whether named fear followed by adult support could be allowed mid-story. One book cannot answer it.
